target_customer: Sales and customer support teams that need fast, current answers from internal knowledge sources
problem: Teams struggle to keep internal knowledge up to date and find answers while working in tools like Zendesk and Salesforce. Omni was a Chrome extension that surfaced short answers from existing knowledge sources.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat subscription (assumed from the product type; not confirmed by a source)

founders.name: Andrew Chang
founders.background_notes: AI and systems focus per the YC page.

competitors.name: Guru
competitors.what: Chrome extension and knowledge base that gave revenue and support teams easy access to company information, launched 2015

technical_complexity.rationale: A browser extension with integrations to several knowledge sources and answer extraction is standard engineering with some NLP work.

defensibility.rationale: An established competitor (Guru) already offered a Chrome extension for the same teams, and a thin extension layer over other tools is easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The YC directory marks Omni acquired, but no acquirer or date was found; the CB Insights claim of an October 2019 Coinbase acquisition predates the batch and was treated as an error.

market_need_then: Support and sales teams were already paying for internal knowledge tools such as Guru, which indicates demand, but no Omni specific evidence of pain or spend was found.

branding.domain_note: Used addomni.com with an add prefix, suggesting omni.com was not available; no purchase story found. The domain failed DNS resolution when checked.

brand_strength.rationale: Search results are dominated by many unrelated products named Omni, including other Chrome extensions and a larger analytics company, and no press about this brand was found.

outcome_analysis: Omni was a five person YC Summer 2020 team building a Chrome extension for internal knowledge answers in a space where Guru already had a similar extension, and where its name collided with many other products called Omni. The YC directory lists it as acquired but the buyer, date and terms are not public in the sources found, so the cause of the exit and whether it was a soft landing cannot be determined. The failure factors are tentative judgments from the crowded market and name collision, not stated causes.
notes: Acquirer and date unknown; the status Acquired comes only from the YC page. CB Insights lists 130000 dollars as a convertible note dated 2020-08-25 from Y Combinator, aggregator only, so no round recorded. A StartupIntros item describing a 1 million dollar Omni seed with Contrary Capital may be a different company and was ignored. RoundFunded data is a reconstruction and was not used. The Guru entry comes from a 2019 Guru launch post and a Chrome Web Store update dated February 2020; Guru's funding then was not checked. The business model line is an assumption flagged as such. The addomni.com site failed to resolve.
